output.subject: Re: CD maturity instructions
output.body:
Dear ⟦CUSTOMER_NAME_1⟧,

Thank you for writing to us, and for your patience and kind words. We have received your complaint, and we want to confirm what you told us.

You mentioned that your 12-month CD matured on September 18, and that about a month before it matured you sent a secure message asking for the proceeds to be moved into your savings account. You told us that the CD instead renewed for another 12 months at 3.10%. You have asked for the funds to be moved to your savings account as you originally requested, without an early withdrawal penalty.

A specialist team is now reviewing your complaint, and we will respond to you within 10 business days. Thank you for letting us know there is no urgency on your end, and we're sorry for the inconvenience this has caused.

If there is anything else you would like us to consider, such as details of the secure message you sent, please reply to this email and we will add it to your complaint.

Kind regards,

Customer Care, Meridian Harbor Bank
notes_for_analyst: Confirm whether the customer's secure message was received about a month before maturity, and what it said.
Decide whether to move the funds to savings and whether to waive the early withdrawal penalty; the draft makes no commitment on either.
Check whether a post-maturity grace period applies that would allow a penalty-free withdrawal, and add it only if confirmed.
Confirm which savings account the customer wants the funds moved to before any transfer.
The draft leaves out the CD balance ($104,250) and account details; add them only if appropriate.
The draft invites the customer to share details of their secure message; remove this if it is not needed.
